newsitem.title: USA: Servico cites hurricane for net income drop.
newsitem.headline: Servico cites hurricane for net income drop.

text.p: Servico Inc said Thursday recurring net income declined because of hurricane and storm activity and the amortization of certain non-cash deferred loan charges.

Earlier, the company reported for the three months ended September 30, 1996, EBITDA of $15.2 million, a 44 percent increase from the $10.5 million reported for the comparable 1995 period. Revenues increased 35 percent to $61.5 million from $45.6 million in the comparable 1995 period.
As previously indicated, recurring net income declined 13 percent, to $1.4 million, or $0.14 per share, from $1.6 million, or $0.16 per share, in the third quarter of 1995.

In the 1996 quarter, Servico incurred losses associated with hurricane and storm activity in the southeastern United States of $186,000, or $0.02 per share, and amortization of certain non-cash deferred loan costs of $642,000, or $0.07 per share.
Weighted average shares outstanding increased 2.6 percent to 9,847,000 from 9,596,000 in the comparable 1995 period.

Recurring income, when combined with the previously announced non-recurring first quarter net gain of $1.7 million and the second quarter extraordinary charge of $202,000, resulted in net income of $6.7 million, or $0.68 per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 1996 as compared with $3.9 million, or $0.42 per share, for the comparable 1995 period. There were 9,728,000 shares outstanding in 1996, a 5.3 percent increase over the 9,238,000 shares outstanding in 1995.

"Although the effect of the amortization of loan costs associated with our May 1996 refinancing reduced quarterly earnings, it had no effect on Servico's fundamental hotel operations and also did not affect our cash position," said David Buddemeyer, president and chief executive.

"EBITDA for both the quarter and year-to-date achieved record levels. Revenue per available room ("REVPAR") at comparable owned hotels increased 3.2 percent for the quarter and 5.4 percent for the nine months over the 1995 comparable periods. We anticipate that our revenue stream and EBITDA will continue to grow in the fourth quarter, moreover, the twelve hotels in which we acquired ownership interests earlier this year will increasingly make positive contributions."
